utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, good morning, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case first of all.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning everyone too. Case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you receiving a translation of the proceedings into your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Be seated again, please. Can I now take the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Mark Harmon appearing with Mr. Fergal Gaynor and Ms. Lise-Lotte Karlsson, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Djuro Cepic, and I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Now, can I ask you first of all if you have got yourself up to speed on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I got short time, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How long have you been involved?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I received supporting material ten days ago, but I'm assigned on 16th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're happy just to proceed in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It wouldn't be a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The case has already involved two counsel, and Mr. Bezbradica submitted a challenge to the indictment. I'm assuming that that is the extent of the preliminary motions which will be involved in the case because time obviously has expired for that. I take it that's the position that you accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I am afraid I need the earphones because the acoustics in this particular court are not great. No, I had removed them. Now, this is a Status Conference affecting one accused out of remaining two in this case. The accused Milan Lukic remains on the indictment but is not at the Tribunal. Mr. Harmon, have you any idea whether and when it's likely that he will be transferred to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't have precise information for you, Your Honour. I am informed that things have progressed nicely in Argentina, that a Judge has signed an order, and I am hopeful -- I'm hopeful that by early next month he will be here, but that's only a speculation. At this point, though, I am assured that matters are moving nicely in Argentina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you will remember the last time we met a brief discussion about the Prosecution's motion to suspend all non-essential proceedings and we agreed to suspend the motion, or at least to suspend consideration of the motion to suspend. I suspect there is no harm done by just leaving that situation be, or do you have anything to say to the contrary?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would leave the situation, Your Honour. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that means that the motion outstanding in this -- well, at least the subject matter outstanding is the form of the indictment, in relation to which there are two motions. Now, I've given consideration to both of these. The Trial Chamber has not yet but will, I think, fairly soon, because the last thing that happened was an order to the Prosecution to clarify certain matters, and the deadline for that's today. Can I take it that deadline will be met?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in that event I would be surprised if we didn't issue a decision in relation to this in the course of next week. The only reason that might change our mind on that would be an indication that there was to be an imminent change in the position of Milan Lukic, but my inclination at the moment is that the Trial Chamber will proceed to deal with the motions that are outstanding in respect of Sredoje Lukic. Now, that takes me, I think, to the question of disclosure, and the supporting material has obviously been disclosed from what Mr. Cepic has said. The only other issue I think I ought to be absolutely clear about is whether your obligations under Rule 68 have been complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's an ongoing obligation, Your Honour, and we will continue to honour the ongoing obligation. We have not complied completely, 100 per cent, with it. As we go through the materials, we will turn it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take it some has been disclosed in terms of Rule 68, or has that not yet begun?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Nothing has.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I hope the idea that this case might be remitted doesn't delay that element of preparation, because whatever happens to the case, whether it's here or elsewhere, that particular obligation will have to be complied with and therefore it might as well be complied with sooner rather than later. I don't want to have to make orders about this. I would rather that as soon as possible there's some clear indication that that obligation is being implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- yes. I accept that as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cepic, is there any matter you wish to raise with me or are there any comments you wish to make on what has gone between Mr. Harmon and myself so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I told you, I just received supporting materials, so I would be very grateful if I received some additional material from Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we've discussed the material that obviously he ought to give you, and you've heard an indication being given that any material which may assist the Defence will now begin to be disclosed to you, and that obligation will be complied with. Is there any other matter you wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what about Mr. Lukic's well-being? Are you satisfied that he is being properly cared for in the Detention Unit and that he has no complaints?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think in light of all that's been said this morning, there's no reason to impose any particular deadline in relation to any matter. I'm relying on the Prosecution to proceed with their obligations of disclosure in accordance with the usual regime without any particular order and as if there was no application to remit the case from the Tribunal. Otherwise, there is nothing that requires a particular deadline to be set today except to indicate when the next Status Conference, if it's necessary, will be held. As long as the case remains here, there will be a Status Conference on the 18th of May. That's the latest date at which it could possibly take place. You should bear that in mind. So if there's any reason when you check later why that may not be possible, then I should be informed immediately. I've set it as late as possible for two reasons; because of the possible arrival of Milan Lukic and also because of the possibility of the case being remitted from the Tribunal. If there's nothing further, then I shall now adjourn the Status Conference.
